questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to a country that was as different as my home country as possible. And I was very excited about the opportunity of going to Istanbul and explore everything that the city had to offer. Moreover, exploring Turkey was also something I had wanted to do for a long time, so it was such a good opportunity to do that.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: During my months in Istanbul, I also realized that living in such a big and chaotic city is perhaps not ideal for me. Living in the city was with many torn feelings, as I on one hand enjoyed all the opportunities, friendships and connections I made there, while I also experienced getting very stressed of how busy the city is.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was so-so, but I found a lot of the information along my way and by talking to the other Erasmus-students + the ESN-network.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I mainly got assistance from the ESN-group at Istanbul University, who were very helpful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found my accommodation through Facebook in advance of my arrival to Istanbul, because I wanted to be sure that I had a place to stay in advance of arriving. However, others had just found temporary accommodation and found more permanent accommodation the first few weeks after the arrival, and they ended up finding both nicer and cheaper accommodation. So my recommendation would be to be patient with the accommodation and not take the first offer available on Facebook, as my experience was that prices there were generally higher.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The city has so many opportunities, so I would definitely recommend living off campus, as there is life everywhere - especially in Besiktas and Kadiköy.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was VERY complicated to put it the least. As an exchange student in anthropology, I was also registered at the faculty, where the department of anthropology is. However, there were no anthropological courses taught in English, and only a few ones at the faculty for political science, which is a different department. I found that the course registration was very confusing and time-consuming, as it was not the easiest to take courses in a different faculty from the one I was registered at.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The professors were helpful in this process. The headmaster of the Department of Anthropology was also helpful, as I felt very sorry that there were no English classes in anthropology (he had not been told that 3 Erasmus exchange students in anthropology were arriving).

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I managed at the end.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be patient and in the end, everything will get solved once you are there.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I found that the level was relatively low for a master's class to be. It felt more like a bachelor's class, and it was sometimes lacking structure. The level of English from the professor's side in one of my classes was also lacking to my experience.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was more just listening to the professor. It was not as engaging as what I have been used to at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1. Theories and Concepts in International Relations
2. Comparative Nationalism and Nation Building

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Theories and Concepts in International Relations was very interesting, and the professor very dedicated with interesting perspectives.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Insurance cost. They only accept insurances in Turkish, so even though I have a global health insurance from Denmark, it was not enough.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Turkish food and transportation is very cheap, while international food is more expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I took part in the ESN-activities, which was a great opportunity to meet other Erasmus students and make friendships - especially in the first month.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Take part in the options that arise.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore the country and get out of Istanbul more than I did - it is nice with breaks from the bustling city.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was so-so. There was first of all a massive language barrier, as the level of English is very, very low. Second of all, I would say that future exchange students should be aware of scams. If you get a Turkish friend, get your Turkish friend to arrange your SIM-card, bureaucracy and purchases that are done at markets, bazaars, etc. The prices are higher for especially Europeans.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Use the app Bumble Friends and settle with the fact that there will probably be a language barrier.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The fact that so many wanted to scam me.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The energy of people and how passionate they can be.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Be patient with the bureaucracy 
- Accept that things are less structured
- Take opportunities to get out of Istanbul during weekends, holidays, etc.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Embrace how spontaneous your life will be.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making all the friendships I did.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Dealing with my housing situation, as I was very unlucky with water leaks, mould and other housing challenges (e.g. a broken vacuum, a broken shower, a broken water pibe).

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
